title: Multimodal LLM-based Agents
reading: The slide contrasts two ways of using a multimodal LLM on the same vision task: building a database of runner faces paired with their bib numbers. The top half shows the non-agentic, zero-shot approach, in which the whole task is issued as a single prompt. The bottom half shows an agentic workflow that decomposes the task into five explicit steps: detect faces as bounding boxes, detect bib numbers as text plus bounding box, match each bib to the nearest face vertically, write a face/bib record to the database, and repeat over all video frames. Accompanying images illustrate the one-shot pass and the iterative loop. Credited to Andrew Ng.

visuals.description: Photograph of a crowd of marathon runners with visible bib numbers, with a downward arrow labelled START at top and FINISH at bottom to its right.
visuals.assertion: The zero-shot workflow goes straight from start to finish in a single uninterrupted pass over the input.

visuals.description: A rounded loop of thick arrows circling a screenshot of Python code (process_image with object_detection calls), labelled 'Coding' on the left arm and 'Planning /Testing' on the right arm.
visuals.assertion: The agentic workflow cycles repeatedly between planning/testing and coding rather than completing in one pass.
